name: APT28
description: APT28 is a long-running cyber espionage unit operated by Russia's GRU military intelligence (Unit 26165). Throughout 2025-2026 the group has run an aggressive, multi-pronged campaign targeting Western logistics and technology firms supporting Ukraine aid shipments, alongside continued spearphishing of Ukrainian government, defense, and prosecutorial bodies. Recent activity includes the new PRISMEX malware family deployed against Ukraine and NATO logistics networks, the LLM-assisted LAMEHUG malware that queries large language models to generate malicious commands on the fly, and rapid same-day exploitation of a newly disclosed Microsoft Office zero-day (CVE-2026-21509). APT28 remains one of the most operationally tempo-heavy and high-profile state APTs given the ongoing war context, combining custom implants (HEADLACE, MASEPIE, OCEANMAP, STEELHOOK, BEARDSHELL, COVENANT) with NTLM-relay credential theft and Exchange mailbox abuse.

ttps.notes: Weaponized Office documents and ZIP/PIF lures (e.g. 'Attachment.pdf.zip') against Ukrainian government and defense bodies
Lures delivered via Signal Desktop, which does not enforce Mark-of-the-Web, bypassing Office macro protections
Exploitation of Outlook CVE-2023-23397 and rapid same-day abuse of new Office zero-day CVE-2026-21509 to leak NTLM hashes
NTLMv2 hash relay attacks via crafted Outlook reminder/task notes and malicious files to capture credentials
Modification of Microsoft Exchange mailbox folder permissions to maintain covert, persistent access to victim mail
Large-scale password spraying and credential guessing against logistics and tech firm webmail/VPN portals
LAMEHUG malware queries an LLM to dynamically generate PowerShell/CMD commands for reconnaissance and exfiltration
MASEPIE and PRISMEX use HTTP(S)-based C2 channels embedded in custom Python and .NET implants

notable_techniques: First confirmed nation-state actor using an LLM at runtime to generate malicious commands (LAMEHUG)
Same-day exploitation of newly disclosed Office zero-day CVE-2026-21509, indicating pre-positioned exploit development
Sustained multi-country espionage campaign against logistics/freight-forwarding firms to track Ukraine aid shipments
Abuse of Signal Desktop attachment handling to bypass Mark-of-the-Web macro protections
Persistent NTLM-relay tradecraft spanning multiple Outlook/Exchange CVEs across years
Targeting of Ukrainian prosecutors and anti-corruption agencies alongside military/defense targets
Use of compromised SOHO/edge routers as anonymization relays for operational infrastructure
detection_opportunities: Monitor for anomalous Exchange mailbox folder permission changes granting external or unusual delegate access
Alert on Outlook items with crafted PidLidReminderFileParameter / task reminder properties referencing UNC paths (CVE-2023-23397 pattern)
Inspect ZIP archives delivered via email containing nested .pif or double-extension executables (e.g. .pdf.zip)
Flag outbound NTLM authentication attempts to external/untrusted hosts (NTLM relay indicators)
Monitor for unusual outbound traffic to LLM API endpoints from endpoints in defense/government networks
Hunt for Signal Desktop-delivered attachments executed without Mark-of-the-Web flags
Apply emergency patching/virtual patching for newly disclosed Office vulnerabilities given APT28's same-day exploitation history
response_playbook: Apply emergency or virtual patching for newly disclosed Office vulnerabilities — APT28 has demonstrated same-day exploitation of new CVEs.
Audit Exchange mailbox folder permissions and delegate access for unauthorized changes.
Flag outbound NTLM authentication attempts to external or untrusted hosts (relay indicators).
Inspect Signal Desktop-delivered attachments for execution without Mark-of-the-Web flags.
Hunt for outbound traffic to LLM API endpoints from defense/government network segments (LAMEHUG indicator).
Review SOHO/edge router configurations for unauthorized changes indicating use as an anonymization relay.
